title: docs(deployment): document the seed/API tenancy repair that rewrites rows at boot
body:
Fixes #9441

Adds `content/docs/deployment/seed-tenancy-repair.mdx` — an operator-facing page for `backfillSeedTenancy`, the one row-rewriting repair on this platform that runs without an operator asking for it.

Docs-only. No behaviour is changed: the card describes a boot-time rewrite with no preview, no flag and no opt-out, and this PR documents what the code does today rather than altering it.

## Every behavioural claim was re-derived from source

Not from the card. Sources read: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/seed-tenancy-backfill.ts`, its `plugin.ts` wiring, `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/duplicates.ts`, and `packages/spec/src/security/tenancy-posture.ts`.

Three places where the source says more than the card did, all now in the page:

**1. There are two triggers, not one.** The card describes the `kernel:ready` boot hook. There is a second call site: `registerSeedTenancyHandoff` in `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts` runs the same repair after any successful `create` on `sys_organization`. On a fresh install that is the **first admin sign-up**, not a boot — and it is the trigger most operators meet first, because at `kernel:ready` on a fresh install no organization exists yet. The boot hook is additionally gated on `environmentId === undefined`, so per-environment (cloud) kernels do not run it at all.

**2. Colliding rows are left untenanted — the stamp excludes them.** The card says already-minted duplicates are "reported, not renumbered", which is true but incomplete. `buildStampSql` adds a `NOT IN` guard per split field, so a row whose identifier is already taken in the target organization is **not moved** and keeps `organization_id = NULL`. The source records why: without the exclusion the whole `UPDATE` violates the partitioned unique index and the driver rolls back everything, including rows that had no conflict.

**3. The two skip paths are distinct.** `skipped-multi-tenant` (posture is `group` or `isolated` — `postureEnforcesWall` is `posture !== 'single'`) and `skipped-ambiguous-organization` (posture is `single` but `sys_organization` does not hold exactly one row) are separate outcomes with separate log lines. The page carries the full six-outcome table and marks which outcomes are silent, because `no-split` writing nothing is the healthy case and is easy to misread as "it did not run".

**No preview, no flag, no opt-out — proven positively.** `grep -rn "process\.env" packages/metadata-protocol/src/` returns only test files plus one unrelated comment; the module takes `(exec, logger)` and no options object. Positive control: the same command shape against `OS_SKIP_MEMBERSHIP_BACKFILL` does find it in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts:951`, so the search would have found a flag had one existed.

## Two PM assumptions, both revisited

**Home: a new page, not `tenancy-modes.mdx`.** Placing this beside the membership backfill would have created the confusion the card exists to remove — an operator reading "Backfill for pre-existing users … opt out with `OS_SKIP_MEMBERSHIP_BACKFILL=1`" immediately followed by a second "backfill" section will reasonably assume one variable governs both. It does not. That page's own frontmatter also scopes it to postures, membership policy and the degraded-boot guard; a row-rewriting data repair is not in it. `content/docs/upgrading.mdx` was the other candidate and is a poorer fit still — it is about the two upgrade clocks, and this repair's most common firing is a first-time sign-up, which is not an upgrade. (It is also at `content/docs/upgrading.mdx`, not under `content/docs/deployment/`.)

So `tenancy-modes.mdx` instead gains a short disambiguation callout that names the two mechanisms as different and states that `OS_SKIP_MEMBERSHIP_BACKFILL` has no effect on this one. That turns the risky adjacency into the disambiguation the card asked for.

**Ordering guidance: kept, and it is useful redundancy rather than a second copy.** The two pages answer different questions from opposite directions. The CLI page answers "I am running this command, what should I know"; this page answers "something rewrote my data, what do I do" — and the operator who most needs the ordering rule is the one who has not yet found the command. Drift risk is low because what is written here is the causal fact (the repair overwrites the `organization_id = NULL` marker and deletes the `__global__` counter row), not the command's flags or output shape, which is the part that would drift.

The page also splits that guidance more precisely than either card did:

- the inventory of identifiers **already** minted twice **survives** the repair, because colliding rows deliberately keep `organization_id = NULL` and therefore stay in two partitions;
- the **live condition** — a `__global__` counter beside an organization-scoped one, the report's only forward-looking line — does **not** survive, because the repair deletes that counter row.

Per the claim comment, `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` is untouched: the reverse cross-reference from the command section is held by PR #9443 and is sequenced separately. This page links to the CLI page without a deep anchor, so nothing breaks before or after that lands.

## Highest-value addition

The multi-organization manual remedy previously existed **only inside a log line**. It is lifted into the page as runnable SQL, with the caveat the log line does not carry: run the inventory first, because if any identifier is held on both sides the `UPDATE` will violate the partitioned unique index and roll back every row including the non-conflicting ones.

## Declared file surface

The claim comment's surface is `content/docs/deployment/**`. One file outside it changed, mechanically and gate-mandated:

- `.claude/workflows/docs-accuracy-audit.js` — `+1` line, the generated scope entry for the new page. `pnpm check:docs-audit-scope` fails without it (observed red: "1 hand-written doc(s) exist but are not listed"), and names its own fix, `check-audit-scope.mjs --write`, which is what produced the line. Without it a run calling itself a "FULL audit" would silently skip the new page. Surface amendment posted on the issue.

## Gates

Union re-derived from the **actual** changed paths with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` after the final commit, which added three families the dispatch list did not name (`check:doc-authoring`, `check:doc-formula-expressions`, `check:skill-frame-sync`) because of the `.claude/` path. All green at `042201f7b`:

```
pnpm check:doc-authoring                                    PASS
pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions  PASS
pnpm check:docs-audit-scope                                 PASS
pnpm check:docs-redirects                                   PASS
pnpm check:role-word                                        PASS
pnpm check:skill-frame-sync                                 PASS
pnpm check:nul-bytes                                        PASS
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:empty-state       PASS
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:liveness          PASS
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:strictness-ledger PASS
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:variant-docs      PASS
```

`check:doc-formula-expressions` was red on first run for an unrelated reason — `@objectstack/formula/dist` was unbuilt in the fresh worktree; `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/lint^...' build` fixed it and it has been green since. Both changed MDX pages were additionally compiled through `@mdx-js/mdx` to confirm the JSX parses.

`skip-changeset`: docs and internal-tooling only, nothing published.
